gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on aurzen.com today the EAZZE D1 MAX (listed at 1,000 ANSI lumens) plus Aurzen's 120-inch screen costs $374.98 together. That is less than the $429.99 Yaber and $469 Wanbo screen bundles ChatGPT showed. It also states no catch: the D1 MAX has no 1/4-inch tripod thread, while the $149.99 EAZZE D1 ($174.98 with the screen) works with Aurzen's foldable stand.
standout_why: I tried to open RTINGS (the page body was cut off), TechRadar (cut off), Crutchfield (403), Travel + Leisure (blocked) and Costco JMGO (429), so I couldn't check what they say. The only rival page I could read, projector-screen-guide.com/projector-and-screen-combo (2026-11-09), gives no prices and names no portable bundle. ChatGPT's own answers quoted single retailer card prices for bundles. None added up a projector plus a separate screen, and none mentioned whether a projector can go on a tripod. I'm scoring this 2, not 3, because I couldn't read most of the rival pages in full.
decides: This backs the page's pick of building the set from separate parts over a boxed bundle: Aurzen's 120-inch screen is $24.99, against $129.99 for Vankyo's own 120-inch screen. It also splits the pick. The D1 + screen at $174.98 is the stand-friendly budget set. The D1 MAX + screen at $374.98 is the bright option, but it needs a ceiling mount (M5 screws), so it isn't a grab-and-go projector. Anyone who needs to run without a wall outlet has to go to the XGIMI MoGo 4 ($479, no screen) or the MoGo 4 Laser Outdoor Collection ($749).
